SIGNED TEMPLATE PACKS
Purpose: Guarantee integrity, provenance, and upgrade safety for all distributed templates.

Signed template packs ensure that what is migrated, scaffolded, or executed is exactly what was authored and approved, with no silent mutation.

CORE GOALS
Integrity

Templates cannot be altered without detection.

Provenance

Every template pack has a known author and origin.

Compatibility Safety

Migration steps are only trusted if signatures validate.

Offline Verifiability

Signature checks do not require network access.

Nyghtshade Enforcement

Signature trust can be role-gated.

PACK FORMAT (CANON)
A signed template pack is a directory or archive with the following structure:

pack.yaml
templates/
  player-movement.yaml
  interaction-raycast.yaml
migrations/
  player-movement.py
  interaction-raycast.py
signature/
  pack.sig
  public.pem
pack.yaml (MANIFEST)
pack:
  id: osl.core
  version: 1.2.0
  engine_support: [unity, unreal]
  created: 2025-12-25
  author: OpenSourceLudus
  license: MIT

integrity:
  hash_algorithm: sha256
  signed_files:
    - templates/player-movement.yaml
    - templates/interaction-raycast.yaml
    - migrations/player-movement.py
This file is always included in the signature.

SIGNATURE MODEL
Cryptography
Algorithm: Ed25519 (fast, modern, deterministic)

Hash: SHA-256

Signature Scope: Entire pack contents (excluding signature directory)

SIGNATURE FILE
signature/pack.sig
Binary signature of the canonical file hash list.

PUBLIC KEY
signature/public.pem
Used for verification only.
Private keys never ship.

VERIFICATION FLOW (CLI & PLUGINS)
Step 1: Hash Validation
Recompute hashes of all declared files

Compare to pack.yaml manifest

Step 2: Signature Validation
Verify hash bundle using public.pem

Reject if invalid

Step 3: Trust Evaluation
Check against:

Local trusted keyring

Nyghtshade role permissions

Registry trust level

Failure at any step aborts execution.

CLI COMMANDS
Verify a pack
osl pack verify ./packs/osl.core
Output:

✔ Hashes valid
✔ Signature valid
✔ Author trusted
Import a pack
osl pack import ./packs/osl.core
Rules:

Verification mandatory

Migration compatibility checked

Stored in local registry mirror

List trusted keys
osl keys list
Trust a key (admin only)
osl keys trust public.pem
FAILURE MODES (HARD)
Signed template packs must fail if:

Any file hash mismatches

Signature invalid or missing

Public key untrusted

Migration chain references unsigned steps

Pack version regresses

No overrides. No warnings. Hard stop.

INTEGRATION WITH MIGRATION SYSTEM
Migration steps must originate from signed packs

Migration execution requires:

Valid signature

Matching pack ID

Compatible template lineage

Unsigned migrations are ignored.

INTEGRATION WITH SCAFFOLD ENGINE
osl scaffold refuses unsigned templates unless:

Explicit --allow-unsigned

Enforcement mode allows it

Nyghtshade mode disallows unsigned scaffolds entirely.

PLUGIN BEHAVIOR (UNITY / UNREAL)
Plugins verify pack signatures before:

Showing diffs

Applying updates

Regenerating code

Unsigned packs are hidden or flagged as unsafe.

CI ENFORCEMENT
Example rule:

fail_if:
  unsigned_templates: true
  unverified_migrations: true
CI must reject builds using unsigned packs.

SECURITY MODEL SUMMARY
Layer	Protection
Hash	File integrity
Signature	Authenticity
Registry	Distribution trust
Migration	Upgrade safety
Nyghtshade	Authority control

Verifiable packs

OFFLINE-FIRST REGISTRY MIRRORING
Purpose: Make templates, migrations, signatures, and trust data fully usable without network access, while remaining cryptographically consistent with upstream sources.

This layer turns OpenSourceLudus into a distributed, resilient system, not a thin client.

1. CORE REQUIREMENTS (CANON)
Offline-first registry mirroring must satisfy all of the following:

No hard dependency on network availability

Deterministic behavior offline

Cryptographic trust preserved offline

Eventual consistency when reconnected

Conflict-safe reconciliation

Nyghtshade enforcement respected locally

If any of these fail, mirroring is invalid.

2. REGISTRY CONCEPT MODEL
There are three registries, conceptually identical but operationally different.

2.1 Upstream Registry (Authoritative)
Remote source

Hosts:

Signed template packs

Public keys

Version metadata

Deprecation markers

2.2 Local Mirror (Authoritative Offline)
Lives on disk

Fully functional without network

Used by:

CLI

Unity plugin

Unreal plugin

CI

2.3 Session Cache (Ephemeral)
Performance optimization

Can be wiped safely

Never trusted alone

3. LOCAL MIRROR LAYOUT (CANON)
~/.osl/registry/
  index.yaml
  packs/
    osl.core/
      1.2.0/
        pack.yaml
        templates/
        migrations/
        signature/
  keys/
    trusted/
      opensourceludus.pem
    revoked/
  metadata/
    sync.log
    last_sync.json
Nothing outside this directory is required for operation.

4. REGISTRY INDEX (index.yaml)
registry:
  schema_version: 1
  last_verified: 2025-12-25T06:42:00Z

packs:
  osl.core:
    latest: 1.2.0
    versions:
      - 1.0.0
      - 1.1.0
      - 1.2.0
This file is the entry point for all lookups.

5. MIRRORING BEHAVIOR
5.1 Startup Resolution Order
Load local mirror

Validate signatures

Validate index integrity

Enforce Nyghtshade access rules

Proceed without network

No network calls occur unless explicitly requested.

5.2 Sync Operation
osl registry sync
Steps:
Fetch upstream index

Compare version sets

Download missing packs

Verify signatures

Update local index

Record sync metadata

Failure Handling:
Partial sync allowed

Corrupt packs rejected

Previous mirror remains valid

5.3 Offline Operation
When offline:

Registry remains fully functional

Scaffolding, migration, diffing all work

No warnings unless explicitly requested

Offline is first-class, not degraded.

6. CONFLICT RESOLUTION RULES
Conflicts are resolved deterministically:

Scenario	Resolution
Same pack ID, different signature	Reject
Same version, different hash	Reject
Local pack newer than upstream	Keep local
Revoked key upstream	Pack invalidated
There is no merge of packs. Packs are immutable.

7. TRUST MODEL (OFFLINE SAFE)
Trusted public keys are stored locally

Revocation lists are cached

Trust decisions do not require live verification

Nyghtshade enforcement applies locally.

Unity / Unreal plugins:
Read only from local mirror

Never fetch directly

Respect local trust + enforcement

Show offline status explicitly

10. CI INTEGRATION
CI jobs:

Use mirrored registry snapshot

Verify no unsigned packs

Enforce migration completeness

No CI job depends on live registry access.

Who can preview

1. CORE PRINCIPLE (CANON)
Preview is informational.
Apply is mutative.
Override is authoritative.
Publish is trust-bearing.

These are four different risk tiers. They are intentionally separated.

No role gets all four by default.

2. CANONICAL ROLES
Nyghtshade defines five roles. You can rename them later, but the capabilities must remain intact.

Role ID	Intended User
observer	Read-only users, QA, auditors
developer	Daily contributors
maintainer	Senior engineers / leads
admin	Project authority
publisher	Registry authority (may be automated)
A single human can hold multiple roles, but permissions are additive, not implicit.

3. PERMISSION MATRIX (THE ANSWER YOU ASKED FOR)
3.1 Who can preview
✅ Everyone

Role	Preview
Observer	✅
Developer	✅
Maintainer	✅
Admin	✅
Publisher	✅
Why:
Preview does not mutate state. Blocking preview creates blind systems and bad decisions.

Preview includes:

Diff UI

Migration simulation

Enforcement warnings

Conflict visibility

Preview never:

Writes files

Alters registry

Executes migrations

3.2 Who can apply
⚠️ Controlled

Role	Apply
Observer	❌
Developer	✅
Maintainer	✅
Admin	✅
Publisher	❌ (unless dual-role)
Apply includes:

Scaffolding

Migration execution

Local file generation

Local registry updates

Constraints:

Apply respects enforcement rules

Apply fails if signatures invalid

Apply blocked if migration gaps exist

Why:
Applying changes alters project state and must be accountable.

3.3 Who can override
🚨 Rare and audited

Role	Override
Observer	❌
Developer	❌
Maintainer	⚠️ Limited
Admin	✅
Publisher	❌
Override means:

Bypassing enforcement failures

Forcing migrations with conflicts

Applying unsigned or future-version templates

Ignoring policy blocks

Rules:

Every override generates an immutable audit record

Overrides require explicit confirmation

Overrides are visible in CI and inspector logs

Why:
Override is where systems break if abused. This power is intentionally narrow.

3.4 Who can publish
🔐 Registry authority only

Role	Publish
Observer	❌
Developer	❌
Maintainer	❌
Admin	❌ (unless delegated)
Publisher	✅
Publish includes:

Signing template packs

Pushing to registry

Bumping canonical versions

Defining migration paths

Important:
Publishing is not a development action. It is a trust action.

Most projects will assign this to:

CI automation

Release managers

A dedicated security role

PHASE A — RBAC ENFORCEMENT MODULE (CLI)
A1. New Module: osl_rbac.py
This module is pure authority logic.
No CLI parsing. No business logic. No I/O beyond config reading.

Its job is to answer exactly one question:

“Is this actor allowed to execute this command, right now?”

A2. Canonical Role Hierarchy (Hard-coded)
ROLE_ORDER = [
    "observer",
    "developer",
    "maintainer",
    "admin",
    "publisher",
]

ROLE_RANK = {role: i for i, role in enumerate(ROLE_ORDER)}
Rules:

Higher rank always includes lower ranks

No dynamic role creation

No aliasing

A3. Command → Required Role Map
COMMAND_REQUIREMENTS = {
    "preview": "observer",
    "list": "observer",
    "export": "observer",

    "apply": "developer",
    "scaffold": "developer",
    "import": "developer",

    "override": "admin",

    "publish": "publisher",
}
Rules:

This table lives in code

CI will validate that every command is listed

Missing entries are build failures

A4. Role Resolution Engine
class RoleContext:
    user: str
    roles: set[str]
    source: str
Resolution order (lowest trust wins):

Explicit CLI flag (--role)

Only allowed if --dev-mode is present

Never allowed in CI

Project config (nyghtshade.roles.yaml)

user: zachary
roles:
  - developer
  - maintainer
Environment variables

NYGHTSHADE_USER=zachary
NYGHTSHADE_ROLE=publisher
Default

observer
Conflict handling:

Multiple roles allowed

Effective role = highest rank role present

Source recorded for audit

A5. Enforcement Function (Single Gate)
def enforce(command: str, ctx: RoleContext) -> None:
    required = COMMAND_REQUIREMENTS[command]
    effective = max(ctx.roles, key=lambda r: ROLE_RANK[r])

    if ROLE_RANK[effective] < ROLE_RANK[required]:
        raise RBACDenied(
            command=command,
            required=required,
            effective=effective,
            roles=ctx.roles,
            source=ctx.source,
        )
This function:

Has no side effects

Throws on failure

Is called before any command logic

A6. RBAC Error Type
class RBACDenied(Exception):
    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "error": "rbac_denied",
            "command": self.command,

        }

GOAL OF REGISTRY RBAC (ABSOLUTE)
The registry must:

Be the final arbiter of truth

Accept input only from trusted actors

Reject all unsigned, unauthorized, or malformed submissions

Preserve immutable history

Remain correct even if every client is compromised

The registry assumes:

CLI may be modified

Plugins may be forked

Users may act maliciously or mistakenly

The registry does not trust intent. It trusts proof.

CORE PRINCIPLE (REGISTRY-SIDE)
If it is not signed, authorized, and auditable, it does not exist.

RBAC enforcement at the registry is non-interactive and non-negotiable.

REGISTRY AUTHORITY MODEL
Canonical Registry Roles
Registry understands only three roles:

Role	Meaning
consumer	Read-only access
publisher	Can publish signed template packs
registry-admin	Infrastructure authority only
All other roles (developer, admin, etc.) do not exist at the registry level.

They must be collapsed into registry roles upstream.

AUTHENTICATION FLOW (HARD GATE)
1. Identity Assertion
Every request must include:

Actor identity

Effective role

Signed assertion token

Example header:

X-Nyghtshade-Identity: zachary
X-Nyghtshade-Role: publisher
X-Nyghtshade-Signature: base64(...)
Unsigned requests are rejected immediately.

2. Role Verification
Registry enforces:

publish endpoint → requires publisher
read endpoint → requires consumer or higher
admin endpoint → requires registry-admin
No fallback. No downgrade. No silent coercion.

3. Signature Validation (MANDATORY)
Every template pack upload must include:

Pack hash

Signature over:

Pack contents

Version

Migration metadata

Publisher identity

Registry verifies:

Signature matches known publisher key

Key has not been revoked

Signature matches payload exactly

Any mismatch → hard reject.

VERSION & MIGRATION ENFORCEMENT
Registry validates:

Version monotonicity

No overwrites

No downgrades

Migration completeness

Every new version includes a valid migration path

No skipped versions

Migration authorization

Certain migrations require elevated publisher privileges

Failure at any step blocks publish.

AUDIT LOGGING (REGISTRY-SIDE)
Registry writes immutable audit records for:

Successful publishes

Failed publishes

Signature failures

Role violations

Migration rejections

Schema (registry-specific):

{
  "timestamp": "2025-12-25T07:02:11Z",
  "actor": "zachary",
  "role": "publisher",
  "action": "publish",
  "package": "unity/player-movement",
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "result": "rejected",
  "reason": "invalid_signature",
  "request_id": "uuid"
}
Registry audit logs are:

Append-only

Immutable

Never rewritten

Exportable for external oversight

FAILURE MODES (INTENTIONAL, CANON)
Registry must reject when:

Role is insufficient

Signature missing or invalid

Pack contents differ from signed hash

Migration chain incomplete

Version already exists

Actor identity unrecognized

There is no override at registry level.

Even registry-admin cannot force publish content.

CLI and plugins are constrained

CI becomes reliable

Offline-first mirroring remains correct

Diff previews reflect canonical truth

Template history is legally and technically defensible

If registry RBAC is weak, everything upstream becomes advisory.

# Quickstart

## Introduction

The Apps SDK relies on the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](/apps-sdk/concepts/mcp-server) to expose your app to ChatGPT. To build an app for ChatGPT with the Apps SDK, you will need two things:

1. A web component built with the framework of your choice – you are free to build your app as you see fit, that will be rendered in an iframe in the ChatGPT interface.
2. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that will be used to expose your app and define your app's capabilities (tools) to ChatGPT.

In this quickstart, we'll build a simple to-do list app, contained in a single HTML file that keeps the markup, CSS, and JavaScript together.

To see more advanced examples using React, see the [examples repository on GitHub](https://github.com/openai/openai-apps-sdk-examples).

## Build a web component

Let's start by creating a file called public/todo-widget.html in a new directory that will be the UI rendered by the Apps SDK in ChatGPT.
This file will contain the web component that will be rendered in the ChatGPT interface.

Add the following content:

html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>Todo list</title>
    <style>
      :root {
        color: #0b0b0f;
        font-family: "Inter", system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
      }

      html,
      body {
        width: 100%;
        min-height: 100%;
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }

      body {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 16px;
        background: #f6f8fb;
      }

      main {
        width: 100%;
        max-width: 360px;
        min-height: 260px;
        margin: 0 auto;
        background: #fff;
        border-radius: 16px;
        padding: 20px;
        box-shadow: 0 12px 24px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.08);
      }

      h2 {
        margin: 0 0 16px;
        font-size: 1.25rem;
      }

      form {
        display: flex;
        gap: 8px;
        margin-bottom: 16px;
      }

      form input {
        flex: 1;
        padding: 10px 12px;
        border-radius: 10px;
        border: 1px solid #cad3e0;
        font-size: 0.95rem;
      }

      form button {
        border: none;
        border-radius: 10px;
        background: #111bf5;
        color: white;
        font-weight: 600;
        padding: 0 16px;
        cursor: pointer;
      }

      input[type="checkbox"] {
        accent-color: #111bf5;
      }

      ul {
        list-style: none;
        padding: 0;
        margin: 0;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        gap: 8px;
      }

      li {
        background: #f2f4fb;
        border-radius: 12px;
        padding: 10px 14px;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 10px;
      }

      li span {
        flex: 1;
      }

      li[data-completed="true"] span {
        text-decoration: line-through;
        color: #6c768a;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <main>
      <h2>Todo list</h2>
      <form id="add-form" autocomplete="off">
        <input id="todo-input" name="title" placeholder="Add a task" />
        <button type="submit">Add</button>
      </form>
      <ul id="todo-list"></ul>
    </main>

    <script type="module">
      const listEl = document.querySelector("#todo-list");
      const formEl = document.querySelector("#add-form");
      const inputEl = document.querySelector("#todo-input");

      let tasks = [...(window.openai?.toolOutput?.tasks ?? [])];

      const render = () => {
        listEl.innerHTML = "";
        tasks.forEach((task) => {
          const li = document.createElement("li");
          li.dataset.id = task.id;
          li.dataset.completed = String(Boolean(task.completed));

          const label = document.createElement("label");
          label.style.display = "flex";
          label.style.alignItems = "center";
          label.style.gap = "10px";

          const checkbox = document.createElement("input");
          checkbox.type = "checkbox";
          checkbox.checked = Boolean(task.completed);

          const span = document.createElement("span");
          span.textContent = task.title;

          label.appendChild(checkbox);
          label.appendChild(span);
          li.appendChild(label);
          listEl.appendChild(li);
        });
      };

      const updateFromResponse = (response) => {
        if (response?.structuredContent?.tasks) {
          tasks = response.structuredContent.tasks;
          render();
        }
      };

      const handleSetGlobals = (event) => {
        const globals = event.detail?.globals;
        if (!globals?.toolOutput?.tasks) return;
        tasks = globals.toolOutput.tasks;
        render();
      };

      window.addEventListener("openai:set_globals", handleSetGlobals, {
        passive: true,
      });

      const mutateTasksLocally = (name, payload) => {
        if (name === "add_todo") {
          tasks = [
            ...tasks,
            { id: crypto.randomUUID(), title: payload.title, completed: false },
          ];
        }

        if (name === "complete_todo") {
          tasks = tasks.map((task) =>
            task.id === payload.id ? { ...task, completed: true } : task
          );
        }

        if (name === "set_completed") {
          tasks = tasks.map((task) =>
            task.id === payload.id
              ? { ...task, completed: payload.completed }
              : task
          );
        }

        render();
      };

      const callTodoTool = async (name, payload) => {
        if (window.openai?.callTool) {
          const response = await window.openai.callTool(name, payload);
          updateFromResponse(response);
          return;
        }

        mutateTasksLocally(name, payload);
      };

      formEl.addEventListener("submit", async (event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const title = inputEl.value.trim();
        if (!title) return;
        await callTodoTool("add_todo", { title });
        inputEl.value = "";
      });

      listEl.addEventListener("change", async (event) => {
        const checkbox = event.target;
        if (!checkbox.matches('input[type="checkbox"]')) return;
        const id = checkbox.closest("li")?.dataset.id;
        if (!id) return;

        if (!checkbox.checked) {
          if (window.openai?.callTool) {
            checkbox.checked = true;
            return;
          }

          mutateTasksLocally("set_completed", { id, completed: false });
          return;
        }

        await callTodoTool("complete_todo", { id });
      });

      render();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>


### Using the Apps SDK in your web component

window.openai is the bridge between your frontend and ChatGPT.

When ChatGPT loads the iframe, it injects the latest tool response into window.openai.toolOutput, which is an object specific to the Apps SDK.
Subsequent calls to window.openai.callTool return fresh structured content so the UI stays in sync.

## Build an MCP server

Install the official Python or Node MCP SDK to create a server and expose a /mcp endpoint.

In this quickstart, we'll use the [Node SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk).

If you're using Python, refer to our [examples repository on GitHub](https://github.com/openai/openai-apps-sdk-examples) to see an example MCP server with the Python SDK.

Install the Node SDK and Zod with:

bash
npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk zod


### MCP server with Apps SDK resources

Register a resource for your component bundle and the tools the model can call (e.g. add_todo and complete_todo) so ChatGPT can drive the UI.

Create a file named server.js and paste the following example that uses the Node SDK:

js






const todoHtml = readFileSync("public/todo-widget.html", "utf8");

const addTodoInputSchema = {
  title: z.string().min(1),
};

const completeTodoInputSchema = {
  id: z.string().min(1),
};

let todos = [];
let nextId = 1;

const replyWithTodos = (message) => ({
  content: message ? [{ type: "text", text: message }] : [],
  structuredContent: { tasks: todos },
});

function createTodoServer() {
  const server = new McpServer({ name: "todo-app", version: "0.1.0" });

  server.registerResource(
    "todo-widget",
    "ui://widget/todo.html",
    {},
    async () => ({
      contents: [
        {
          uri: "ui://widget/todo.html",
          mimeType: "text/html+skybridge",
          text: todoHtml,
          _meta: { "openai/widgetPrefersBorder": true },
        },
      ],
    })
  );

  server.registerTool(
    "add_todo",
    {
      title: "Add todo",
      description: "Creates a todo item with the given title.",
      inputSchema: addTodoInputSchema,
      _meta: {
        "openai/outputTemplate": "ui://widget/todo.html",
        "openai/toolInvocation/invoking": "Adding todo",
        "openai/toolInvocation/invoked": "Added todo",
      },
    },
    async (args) => {
      const title = args?.title?.trim?.() ?? "";
      if (!title) return replyWithTodos("Missing title.");
      const todo = { id: `todo-${nextId++}`, title, completed: false };
      todos = [...todos, todo];
      return replyWithTodos(`Added "${todo.title}".`);
    }
  );

  server.registerTool(
    "complete_todo",
    {
      title: "Complete todo",
      description: "Marks a todo as done by id.",
      inputSchema: completeTodoInputSchema,
      _meta: {
        "openai/outputTemplate": "ui://widget/todo.html",
        "openai/toolInvocation/invoking": "Completing todo",
        "openai/toolInvocation/invoked": "Completed todo",
      },
    },
    async (args) => {
      const id = args?.id;
      if (!id) return replyWithTodos("Missing todo id.");
      const todo = todos.find((task) => task.id === id);
      if (!todo) {
        return replyWithTodos(`Todo ${id} was not found.`);
      }

      todos = todos.map((task) =>
        task.id === id ? { ...task, completed: true } : task
      );

      return replyWithTodos(`Completed "${todo.title}".`);
    }
  );

  return server;
}

const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8787);
const MCP_PATH = "/mcp";

const httpServer = createServer(async (req, res) => {
  if (!req.url) {
    res.writeHead(400).end("Missing URL");
    return;
  }

  const url = new URL(req.url, `http://${req.headers.host ?? "localhost"}`);

  if (req.method === "OPTIONS" && url.pathname === MCP_PATH) {
    res.writeHead(204, {
      "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
      "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "POST, GET, OPTIONS",
      "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "content-type, mcp-session-id",
      "Access-Control-Expose-Headers": "Mcp-Session-Id",
    });
    res.end();
    return;
  }

  if (req.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/") {
    res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "text/plain" }).end("Todo MCP server");
    return;
  }

  const MCP_METHODS = new Set(["POST", "GET", "DELETE"]);
  if (url.pathname === MCP_PATH && req.method && MCP_METHODS.has(req.method)) {
    res.setHeader("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*");
    res.setHeader("Access-Control-Expose-Headers", "Mcp-Session-Id");

    const server = createTodoServer();
    const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({
      sessionIdGenerator: undefined, // stateless mode
      enableJsonResponse: true,
    });

    res.on("close", () => {
      transport.close();
      server.close();
    });

    try {
      await server.connect(transport);
      await transport.handleRequest(req, res);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error("Error handling MCP request:", error);
      if (!res.headersSent) {
        res.writeHead(500).end("Internal server error");
      }
    }
    return;
  }

  res.writeHead(404).end("Not Found");
});

httpServer.listen(port, () => {
  console.log(
    `Todo MCP server listening on http://localhost:${port}${MCP_PATH}`
  );
});


This snippet also responds to GET / for health checks, handles CORS preflight for /mcp and nested routes like /mcp/actions, and returns 404 Not Found for OAuth discovery routes you are not using yet. That keeps ChatGPT’s connector wizard from surfacing 502 errors while you iterate without authentication.

## Run locally

If you're using a web framework like React, build your component into static assets so the HTML template can inline them.
Usually, you can run a build command such as npm run build to produce a dist directory with your compiled assets.

In this quickstart, since we're using vanilla HTML, no build step is required.

Start the MCP server on http://localhost:<port>/mcp from the directory that contains server.js (or server.ts).

Make sure you have "type": "module" in your package.json file:

json
{
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.20.2",
    "zod": "^3.25.76"
  }
}


Then run the server with the following command:

bash
node server.js


The server should print Todo MCP server listening on http://localhost:8787/mcp once it is ready.

### Test with MCP Inspector

You can use the [MCP Inspector](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/inspector) to test your server locally.

bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest http://localhost:8787/mcp


This will open a browser window with the MCP Inspector interface. You can use this to test your server and see the tool responses.

![MCP Inspector](/images/apps-sdk/mcp_inspector.png)

### Expose your server to the public internet

For ChatGPT to access your server during development, you need to expose it to the public internet. You can use a tool such as [ngrok](https://ngrok.com/) to open a tunnel to your local server.

bash
ngrok http <port>


This will give you a public URL like https://<subdomain>.ngrok.app that you can use to access your server from ChatGPT.

When you add you connector, provide the public URL with the /mcp path (e.g. https://<subdomain>.ngrok.app/mcp).

## Add your app to ChatGPT

Once you have your MCP server and web component working locally, you can add your app to ChatGPT with the following steps:

1. Enable [developer mode](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/developer-mode) under **Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings** in ChatGPT.
2. Click the **Create** button to add a connector under **Settings → Connectors** and paste the HTTPS + /mcp URL from your tunnel or deployment (e.g. https://<subdomain>.ngrok.app/mcp).
3. Name the connector, provide a short description and click **Create**.

<div style={{ width: "50%", margin: "0 auto", display: "block" }}>
  <img
    src="/images/apps-sdk/new_connector.jpg"
    alt="Add your connector to ChatGPT"
  />
</div>

4. Open a new chat, add your connector from the **More** menu (accessible after clicking the **+** button), and prompt the model (e.g., “Add a new task to read my book”). ChatGPT will stream tool payloads so you can confirm inputs and outputs.

![Add your connector to a conversation](/images/apps-sdk/developer_mode_more.jpg)

You said:
WHY DOSE IT GO BACK QND FORTH FROM CPU TO MEM IN RED LIGHTS 
ChatGPT said:
Short answer: those red lights mean your motherboard is failing its power-on self-test and bouncing between CPU and RAM checks. It is not random. It is diagnostic.

Here’s what is actually happening, step by step.

WHAT THE CPU ↔ RAM RED LIGHT LOOP MEANS
Most modern motherboards have debug LEDs labeled something like:

CPU

DRAM / MEM

VGA

BOOT

On startup, the board checks hardware in order. If a step fails, it stops or loops.

When you see it flip back and forth between CPU and MEM, it means:

The CPU cannot successfully initialize the memory controller.

And that controller lives inside the CPU, not the motherboard.

So the board keeps retrying:

Power CPU

CPU tries to train RAM

RAM init fails

Board resets CPU

Repeat

That loop is the red lights you’re seeing.

THE MOST COMMON CAUSES (IN ORDER OF LIKELIHOOD)
1️⃣ RAM TRAINING FAILURE (MOST COMMON)
This happens when:

RAM speed is too high for first boot

XMP/EXPO is unstable

RAM isn’t fully seated

RAM is in the wrong slots

Fix

Power off

Pull RAM

Install one stick only

Use the primary slot (usually A2)

Clear CMOS

Boot at default speed

2️⃣ BIOS DOES NOT SUPPORT THE CPU
Very common with:

Ryzen upgrades

Newer CPUs on older boards

Symptoms:

CPU light → RAM light → CPU light loop

No video output

Fans spin but nothing progresses

Fix

Flash the latest BIOS

Use BIOS Flashback if available

Do NOT rely on “it should support it”

If the CPU microcode isn’t there, RAM will never train.

3️⃣ CPU SEATING OR SOCKET ISSUE
If even one pin or pad is wrong:

Memory controller fails

Board cannot determine RAM timings

Fix

Remove CPU

Inspect pins carefully

Reseat CPU evenly

Do not overtighten cooler

Overtightened coolers absolutely can cause this.

4️⃣ Incompatible RAM KIT
Even “supported” RAM can fail if:

Mixed kits

Different revisions

High-density DIMMs

Fix

Test with known-good, low-speed RAM (DDR4-2133 / DDR5-4800)

Avoid RGB RAM during troubleshooting

5️⃣ Power Delivery Instability
Less common, but real:

Weak PSU

Missing EPS CPU cable

Bad 8-pin connection

Fix

Ensure CPU power cable is connected

Do not use split cables if avoidable

Reseat PSU cables

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE “CPU ↔ RAM ARGUMENT”
Because that’s exactly what it is:

The CPU owns memory initialization

The motherboard owns retry logic

When training fails, the board resets the CPU

The CPU retries memory

Failure loops

Nothing else can happen until RAM trains successfully.

WHAT IT IS NOT
Not GPU related

Not storage related

Not Windows

Not drivers

Not “just a bad board” (usually)

This is pre-boot hardware negotiation.

Before you can find a BIOS update for your board, you need to know the exact model name and revision of that MSI motherboard. Here’s the detailed process to identify the board and then update its BIOS:

1) Identify Your Exact Motherboard Model
The BIOS version string you saw isn’t enough to locate the right download. You must find the model number like B150-M Mortar, Z170-A PRO, etc. Options:

A. Check the board physically

Look on the PCB near the CPU socket or PCIe slots.

It typically says something like “MS-XXXX” or the board product name printed in white text. 
account.msi.com

B. Look in BIOS

Boot into BIOS → often on the first screen it shows the board name/model.

If not obvious, some BIOS screens show “Product Name” or similar.

C. Use Windows system tools

Press Win+R → type msinfo32 → Enter.

In the System Information window look for BaseBoard Manufacturer/Model or BIOS Version/Date. 
MSI Global English Forum

Without knowing exactly what board you have, you cannot safely download the correct BIOS. MSI BIOS files are model-specific.

2) Find and Download the Latest BIOS
Once you have the exact model name:

Go to MSI’s official support site:
https://www.msi.com/support

Enter your board’s model name in the search box.

Select your exact board from the list.

Go to the “BIOS” section.

Download the latest BIOS file for your board and revision.
Do not use a BIOS intended for a different board, even if the filename looks similar.

This matches MSI’s official update process. 
MSI USA

3) Prepare a USB Flash Drive for BIOS Update
BIOS updates on MSI boards are typically done via the M-FLASH utility in the BIOS:

Format a USB drive to FAT32.

Extract the BIOS ZIP you downloaded.

Copy the BIOS file to the USB’s root directory (no folders).

Boot into BIOS and use M-FLASH to select and apply the BIOS file.
Do not interrupt the flashing process. 
MSI USA

Alternative: some MSI systems allow updating via Windows or MSI Center, but manually using M-FLASH is more reliable by far. 
Reddit

Updating the BIOS after identifying the correct board model will let the board properly train modern DDR4 and stop strange RAM training behavior.

I’ll break this down cleanly and thoroughly so you know exactly what you’re looking at and why it exists.

Visual reference (to anchor what you’re seeing)

1️⃣ The narrow ~13-pin connector on the back side of the PCB
What it is
That small rectangular connector with ~13 pins is an internal expansion header, specifically for professional sync / video I/O add-ons.

On the Quadro K4000, this is used for:

SDI (Serial Digital Interface) output cards

Genlock / Framelock synchronization modules

Broadcast and film pipeline hardware

What it is not
❌ Not PCIe

❌ Not memory

❌ Not power

❌ Not something a normal PC ever uses

Why it exists
Quadro cards are designed for:

Video walls

Film production

Broadcast studios

Medical imaging

Simulation environments

In those environments, multiple GPUs must output frames at the exact same time, down to microseconds. That connector allows:

Frame-accurate synchronization

Locking GPU output to external clocks

Feeding raw video signals to broadcast equipment

Can you use it?
For a normal PC, game dev, Unity, Unreal, or desktop use:

No. Completely ignore it.

It requires:

Proprietary NVIDIA expansion hardware

Special drivers

Studio equipment

Software you will never run at home

Leaving it unused is expected.

2️⃣ The 4-pin connector near the exhaust vent
What it is
That 4-pin connector is an auxiliary power input, but not the standard PCIe 6-pin or 8-pin you’re used to.

It is:

A proprietary workstation power connector

Intended for OEM systems (HP, Dell, Lenovo workstations)

Why it exists
In enterprise workstations:

Power is delivered through custom harnesses

GPUs sometimes receive power from internal board rails, not PSU cables

This improves airflow and reliability in dense chassis

Some Quadro K4000 variants:

Use only PCIe slot power

Others optionally accept this 4-pin auxiliary input

Important clarification
That connector is not required unless:

The card is installed in a workstation that provides it

The system specifically expects it

In a standard ATX PC:

If the card posts and displays without it, you’re fine

Do not try to adapt random cables into it

Do not connect a CPU fan header to it

Electrical reality
The K4000 is a ~80W card

PCIe slot provides up to 75W

The auxiliary connector is there for margin and stability in OEM systems

3️⃣ The “two tabs” you mentioned on the PCIe edge
Just to clear this up:

Those are mechanical retention notches

One aligns with PCIe x16

The other helps stabilize the card in workstation backplanes

They are not electrical contacts.

4️⃣ Why consumer GPUs don’t have this stuff
A GTX 1660 Super:

Outputs frames whenever it feels like

Doesn’t sync with external clocks

Doesn’t talk to broadcast gear

Doesn’t care about genlock

A Quadro:

Must obey external timing

Must integrate with other machines

Must not drift a single frame over hours

That’s why it has:

Extra headers

Sync ports

Weird connectors

Enterprise-only features

5️⃣ Practical advice for your setup
For your MSI board + i5-6400 + dev usage:

Ignore the 13-pin header

Ignore the 4-pin auxiliary connector unless required

Do not attempt to adapt or “try” cables

Use the GTX 1660 Super instead for Unity/Unreal

The Quadro K4000 is fascinating hardware, but it belongs to:

2012–2014 workstation workflows

CAD desks

Editing bays

Simulation labs

Not modern game engines.

Bottom line
13-pin connector → professional sync / SDI / genlock expansion

4-pin connector → OEM workstation auxiliary power

Both are normal for Quadro

Neither is useful for a home dev PC

Nothing is missing or broken

ChatGPT said:
Yeah, that’s a very common trap, and you’re not wrong to think it looks like a fan header. Physically, it absolutely does. Electrically and functionally, it is not the same thing, and plugging a fan cable into it is one of those “instant regret” moves.

Here’s the clean breakdown.

Why it looks like a fan header
Same 4-pin JST/Molex-style housing

Same pin spacing

Same location near airflow/exhaust

NVIDIA did not help anyone by reusing a familiar connector shape. OEMs love standard-looking parts even when they’re not standard.

Why it is not a fan header
A standard PC fan header:
12V (regulated)

Ground

Tach (RPM sense)

PWM control

Very low current

Driven by motherboard fan controller

The Quadro K4000 4-pin connector:
Auxiliary power input

No PWM

No tach

No fan control logic

Designed to feed power into the GPU, not control anything

Internally, that connector ties into the GPU’s power delivery circuitry, not a controller.

What happens if you plug a fan into it
Best case:

Fan does nothing

System fails to POST

GPU doesn’t initialize

Worst case:

You backfeed voltage into the GPU

Blow a VRM phase

Kill the card instantly

Possibly damage the motherboard slot

There’s no “it’ll probably be fine” here. It’s one of those don’t try it once situations.

What happens if you plug a motherboard fan header into it
Same problem, reversed direction:

Motherboard outputs control signals

GPU expects power

Signals go nowhere useful

Risk of short or logic damage

Again: bad idea.

Why NVIDIA did this
This connector exists for OEM workstation chassis where:

The PSU does not use standard PCIe cables

Power is delivered via internal harnesses

GPUs are fed from a distribution board

Fans are managed separately

Dell, HP, Lenovo workstations all do this kind of thing.

In those systems:

That connector plugs into a custom power rail

It is not optional

The card may refuse to boot without it

In a normal ATX PC:

The card relies entirely on PCIe slot power

The connector is unused

This is expected behavior

How to tell if your card needs it
Simple rule:

If the card posts and displays without it → ignore it

If the card refuses to initialize → it came from an OEM system that expected that power rail

Most Quadro K4000 retail cards:

Do not require it

It’s there “just in case”

Final safety rule (burn this in)
If it looks like a fan header but is on a GPU, assume it is NOT a fan header unless the manual explicitly says so.

You did the right thing by stopping and asking instead of “eh, let’s see what happens.”

You said:
Okay on the Tomahawk B450 there are two M.2 slots. Will either of those take a SSD SATA hard drive?
ChatGPT said:
Short answer: one of them can, one of them can’t.
Long answer below so you don’t accidentally buy the wrong drive or stick something in the wrong slot.

MSI B450 Tomahawk — M.2 reality check
The B450 Tomahawk has two M.2 slots, but they are not equal.

🔹 M.2 Slot #1 (top slot, near the CPU)
Supports:

NVMe (PCIe 3.0 x4) ✅

M.2 SATA SSDs ✅

Key type: M-key

Common sizes: 2242 / 2260 / 2280

👉 This slot is the most flexible.
If you have an M.2 SATA SSD, this is the slot you want.

⚠️ Important side effect:

Using an M.2 SATA drive here disables one SATA port on the motherboard (usually SATA5 or SATA6). That’s normal.

🔹 M.2 Slot #2 (bottom slot, near the chipset)
Supports:

NVMe (PCIe) ✅

M.2 SATA SSDs ❌ NO

Key type: M-key

PCIe lanes: Shared with chipset resources

👉 This slot is NVMe-only.
A SATA M.2 drive will not be detected here at all.

Quick compatibility table
Drive type	M.2 Slot 1	M.2 Slot 2
M.2 NVMe	✅ Yes	✅ Yes
M.2 SATA	✅ Yes	❌ No
2.5" SATA SSD	❌ No (needs cable)	❌ No
How to tell what kind of M.2 drive you have
Look at the label or model number:

SATA M.2 usually says:

“SATA”

“AHCI”

Speeds around 500–550 MB/s

NVMe M.2 usually says:

“NVMe”

“PCIe”

Speeds 1500 MB/s+

If it’s SATA and you put it in Slot #2 → it won’t show up anywhere, not BIOS, not Windows.

Practical advice
If you’re reusing older hardware or budget drives → use M.2 Slot #1

If you’re installing a modern NVMe SSD → either slot works

Don’t force a SATA M.2 into Slot #2 and assume it’s dead — it isn’t, it’s just incompatible there

Bottom line
✔ Yes, the B450 Tomahawk can take an M.2 SATA SSD
❌ Only in the top M.2 slot
✔ Bottom slot is NVMe-only

If you want, tell me the exact SSD model number and I’ll tell you instantly:

Which slot to use

Which SATA port gets disabled

Best BIOS setting to flip if needed

Short answer first, then the “why,” because this stuff is needlessly confusing on purpose.

MSI B450 Tomahawk – M.2 + SATA compatibility
Yes — one of the M.2 slots on the MSI B450 Tomahawk can take an M.2 SATA SSD, but not both in the same way.

Here’s the exact breakdown.

🔹 The two M.2 slots on the B450 Tomahawk
M2_1 (top slot, near the CPU)
Supports:

NVMe (PCIe 3.0 x4)

M.2 SATA

This slot is the most flexible.

If you plug an M.2 SATA drive here, it will work as long as the linked SATA port is not in use.

⚠️ Using an M.2 SATA drive here disables one of the SATA ports (usually SATA5 or SATA6).

M2_2 (bottom slot, near PCIe slots)
Supports:

NVMe (PCIe only)

❌ Does NOT support M.2 SATA

If you put an M.2 SATA SSD here, it will:

Not show in BIOS

Not show in Windows

Make you question reality

🔹 About the SSD in your photos
From the images you posted:

That drive is M.2 SATA, not NVMe

You can tell because:

Single notch (B+M key)

Controller layout matches SATA-based M.2

No large NVMe controller + DRAM layout typical of PCIe drives

So:

✅ It will work in M2_1
❌ It will NOT work in M2_2

🔹 BIOS setting you may need
If it doesn’t show immediately:

Enter BIOS

Go to Advanced → Integrated Peripherals

Make sure:

M.2/Optane Genie = Disabled

SATA mode = AHCI

Save and reboot

Then check Disk Management in Windows and initialize it if needed.

🔹 Common gotchas (aka “why people hate M.2”)
M.2 SATA ≠ NVMe, even though they look identical

Slot support depends on chipset routing, not physical size

Using M.2 SATA disables a SATA port silently

Older BIOS versions sometimes fail to enumerate M.2 SATA properly (you already fixed this by flashing)

🧠 Bottom line
Yes, your B450 Tomahawk can use that SSD

Only in the top M.2 slot (M2_1)

Expect one SATA port to be disabled

The drive itself looks fine

You didn’t buy junk. The board is just picky and passive-aggressive about storage.

STEP 2: DEFINE TIME VARIABLES (C++)
In NH_GameState.h:

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/GameStateBase.h"
#include "NH_GameState.generated.h"

UCLASS()
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_GameState : public AGameStateBase
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    ANH_GameState();

    virtual void Tick(float DeltaTime) override;

    // Time values
    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentHour;

    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentMinute;

    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    float TimeScale;

protected:
    float MinuteAccumulator;
};
What this means in human terms:

TimeScale: how fast time passes (1 real second = X in-game minutes)

MinuteAccumulator: prevents jitter and chaos

STEP 3: IMPLEMENT TIME FLOW
In NH_GameState.cpp:

#include "NH_GameState.h"

ANH_GameState::ANH_GameState()
{
    PrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = true;

    CurrentHour = 6;
    CurrentMinute = 0;
    TimeScale = 60.0f; // 1 real second = 1 in-game minute
    MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;
}

void ANH_GameState::Tick(float DeltaTime)
{
    Super::Tick(DeltaTime);

    MinuteAccumulator += DeltaTime * TimeScale;

    if (MinuteAccumulator >= 60.0f)
    {
        MinuteAccumulator -= 60.0f;
        CurrentMinute++;

        if (CurrentMinute >= 60)
        {
            CurrentMinute = 0;
            CurrentHour++;

            if (CurrentHour >= 24)
            {
                CurrentHour = 0;
            }
        }
    }
}
This is not fancy.
It is reliable, which is more important.

Now Unreal actually uses your clock instead of pretending.

Corrected Header (final version)
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/GameStateBase.h"
#include "NH_GameState.generated.h"

DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_TwoParams(
    FOnNHMinuteChanged,
    int32, Hour,
    int32, Minute
);

/**
 * Global game clock. Ticks in minutes and broadcasts minute changes.
 */
UCLASS()
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_GameState : public AGameStateBase
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    ANH_GameState();

    virtual void Tick(float DeltaSeconds) override;
    virtual void BeginPlay() override;

    // Current in-game time
    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentHour = 6;

    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentMinute = 0;

    // In-game minutes advanced per real second.
    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category="Time")
    float TimeScale = 1.0f;

    // Fired after time updates
    UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable, Category="Time")
    FOnNHMinuteChanged OnMinuteChanged;

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Time")
    void SetTime(int32 Hour, int32 Minute);

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Time")
    void GetTime(int32& OutHour, int32& OutMinute) const;

protected:
    float MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;
};
The Missing .cpp (This Is the Engine)
Create NH_GameState.cpp and paste this exactly.

#include "NH_GameState.h"

ANH_GameState::ANH_GameState()
{
    PrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = true;
    PrimaryActorTick.bStartWithTickEnabled = true;
}

void ANH_GameState::BeginPlay()
{
    Super::BeginPlay();
    MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;
}

void ANH_GameState::Tick(float DeltaSeconds)
{
    Super::Tick(DeltaSeconds);

    if (TimeScale <= 0.f)
    {
        return;
    }

    MinuteAccumulator += DeltaSeconds * TimeScale;

    while (MinuteAccumulator >= 1.0f)
    {
        MinuteAccumulator -= 1.0f;
        CurrentMinute++;

        if (CurrentMinute >= 60)
        {
            CurrentMinute = 0;
            CurrentHour = (CurrentHour + 1) % 24;
        }

        OnMinuteChanged.Broadcast(CurrentHour, CurrentMinute);
    }
}

void ANH_GameState::SetTime(int32 Hour, int32 Minute)
{
    CurrentHour = FMath::Clamp(Hour, 0, 23);
    CurrentMinute = FMath::Clamp(Minute, 0, 59);
    MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;

    OnMinuteChanged.Broadcast(CurrentHour, CurrentMinute);
}

void ANH_GameState::GetTime(int32& OutHour, int32& OutMinute) const
{
    OutHour = CurrentHour;
    OutMinute = CurrentMinute;
}
Why This Version Is Correct
Uses while, not if, so low FPS doesn’t desync time

Broadcasts after time changes

Safe against TimeScale = 0

Blueprint-friendly

Deterministic

This clock is now authoritative enough to run:

NPC schedules

Shift changes

Lockdowns

Meals

Story triggers

NYGHTSHADE HOLLOW
CORE SYSTEM 01: TIME MANAGER (UNREAL ENGINE)
This is the authoritative clock. Nothing argues with it. NPCs, jobs, meals, lockdowns, dialogue, all bow to time.

WHAT THIS SYSTEM MUST DO
Non-negotiable requirements:

Track in-game time (hours + minutes)

Advance time consistently

Broadcast time changes to other systems

Be globally accessible

Be save/load friendly later

No UI yet. No fancy sun cycles. We’re not painting flames on an engine that isn’t running.

ARCHITECTURE DECISION (IMPORTANT)
We put this in the GameState, not a random actor.

Why:

Exists on every level

Designed to hold game-wide state

Correct place for “the world knows this” data

STEP 1: CREATE THE TIME MANAGER CLASS
Unreal Editor
Create C++ Class

Parent class: GameStateBase

Name it:
NH_GameState

This becomes the brainstem.

STEP 2: DEFINE TIME VARIABLES (C++)
In NH_GameState.h:

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/GameStateBase.h"
#include "NH_GameState.generated.h"

UCLASS()
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_GameState : public AGameStateBase
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    ANH_GameState();

    virtual void Tick(float DeltaTime) override;

    // Time values
    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentHour;

    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentMinute;

    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    float TimeScale;

protected:
    float MinuteAccumulator;
};
What this means in human terms:

TimeScale: how fast time passes (1 real second = X in-game minutes)

MinuteAccumulator: prevents jitter and chaos

STEP 3: IMPLEMENT TIME FLOW
In NH_GameState.cpp:

#include "NH_GameState.h"

ANH_GameState::ANH_GameState()
{
    PrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = true;

    CurrentHour = 6;
    CurrentMinute = 0;
    TimeScale = 60.0f; // 1 real second = 1 in-game minute
    MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;
}

void ANH_GameState::Tick(float DeltaTime)
{
    Super::Tick(DeltaTime);

    MinuteAccumulator += DeltaTime * TimeScale;

    if (MinuteAccumulator >= 60.0f)
    {
        MinuteAccumulator -= 60.0f;
        CurrentMinute++;

        if (CurrentMinute >= 60)
        {
            CurrentMinute = 0;
            CurrentHour++;

            if (CurrentHour >= 24)
            {
                CurrentHour = 0;
            }
        }
    }
}
This is not fancy.
It is reliable, which is more important.

STEP 4: REGISTER GAMESTATE
This is where people forget a step and spiral.

Open Project Settings

Go to Maps & Modes

Set:

Game State Class → NH_GameState

Now Unreal actually uses your clock instead of pretending.

STEP 5: BLUEPRINT ACCESS (CRITICAL)
You want designers, AI, and future-you to read time without crying.

In Blueprint:

Read:

CurrentHour

CurrentMinute

That’s it. No event spaghetti yet.

BP_NPC_Inmate_01 EventGraph (pseudocode nodes)

Event BeginPlay
Get Controlled Pawn (self)
Get NH_ScheduleComponent (Get Component by class OR drag the component into graph)
Bind Event to OnScheduleUpdated (OnScheduleUpdated is the delegate from UNH_ScheduleComponent)
Drag from NH_ScheduleComponent -> Bind Event to OnScheduleUpdated -> Create custom event: OnScheduleUpdated_Event (Activity, TargetActor)
From OnScheduleUpdated_Event:
Get Controller -> Cast to NH_SimpleAIController (or to AIController)
From the Controller, Get Blackboard (if you used a BT with BlackboardComponent; in blueprint you can use GetBlackboard or "Get Blackboard" node from AIController)
Set Value as Object (KeyName = "TargetActor", Value = TargetActor)
Set Value as Name (KeyName = "Activity", Value = Activity)
Optionally, if Controller is not running the BT, call Run Behavior Tree (supply BT_NPC_Inmate) once.
Detailed node wiring instructions (node sequence)

In Graph: Add node Event BeginPlay.
From BeginPlay -> Get NH_ScheduleComponent (drag component into graph).
Drag off NH_ScheduleComponent -> "Bind Event to OnScheduleUpdated" -> create custom event OnScheduleUpdated_Event.
The custom event will have two inputs: Activity (Name) and TargetActor (Actor).
From OnScheduleUpdated_Event -> Get Controller (GetController) -> Cast To NH_SimpleAIController (or cast to AIController).
From Cast -> Get Blackboard (use "Get Blackboard" on the Controller or use "Get Blackboard Value as Object/Name" nodes).
Use "Set Value as Object" node (from Blackboard) — Key Name: TargetActor — Value: TargetActor input from the event.
Use "Set Value as Name" — Key Name: Activity — Value: Activity input.
(Optional) On BeginPlay ensure the Behavior Tree is running:
On BeginPlay -> Get Controller -> Cast -> Run Behavior Tree (BT_NPC_Inmate).
Alternatively, add a blueprint variable in the Character: BehaviorTree (Object Reference) and assign BT_NPC_Inmate, then call Run Behavior Tree with it.
Step F — How the ScheduleComponent updates the blackboard in practice

When the game clock advances and the NH_ScheduleComponent determines a new schedule row, it fires OnScheduleUpdated(ActivityName, TargetActor).
The BP_NPC_Inmate_01 binding (above) sets the Blackboard keys; the Behavior Tree sees the changed TargetActor and will start MoveTo(TargetActor).
When the activity ends and a new TargetActor is set, the BT MoveTo will interrupt/re-plan accordingly.
Step G — Create debug widget (BP_ScheduleDebug) and auto-add to viewport Create a simple UMG widget to show current time and the NPC’s Activity.

UMG creation steps

Content Browser → Right click → User Interface → Widget Blueprint → name it WBP_ScheduleDebug.
Open WBP_ScheduleDebug Designer:
Add Vertical Box.
Add Text Block: give it name TB_Time (this will show Hour:Minute).
Add Text Block: give it name TB_NPCActivity (this will show NPC current Activity).
In Graph of WBP_ScheduleDebug:
Create a custom event UpdateDebug.
In UpdateDebug:
Get Game State -> Cast to ANH_GameState -> Get CurrentHour/CurrentMinute
Format text: e.g., Hour:Minute (pad minute with two digits)
Set TB_Time -> SetText (the formatted string)
Also get reference to NPC actor (drag a variable NPCReference of type Actor and set it in Level Blueprint when adding widget).
From NPCReference -> Get NH_ScheduleComponent -> (if you added a Blueprint getter for current activity on the component, call it; otherwise capture the current Activity by binding to OnScheduleUpdated to set a variable on the NPC BP that the widget reads)
Set TB_NPCActivity -> SetText (ActivityName)
Create a Tick (Event Tick) or Timer (every 0.5s) to call UpdateDebug (Timer is better than Tick).
Level Blueprint: On BeginPlay
Create Widget -> Class = WBP_ScheduleDebug -> Return Value widget
Add to Viewport
(Optional) Set the widget’s NPCReference variable: Get All Actors of Class (BP_NPC_Inmate_01) -> Get(0) -> Set widget variable NPCReference.
Alternative simpler approach for Activity value:

In BP_NPC_Inmate_01, when OnScheduleUpdated runs, set a public variable CurrentActivity (Name). The widget can Get All Actors of Class (BP_NPC_Inmate_01) -> Get(0) -> Get CurrentActivity and use it for display.

F) How the pieces interact (summary)

NH_GameState broadcasts minute ticks.
UNH_ScheduleComponent listens and sets CurrentActivity / CurrentTargetActor and calls OnScheduleUpdated which BP binds to and writes to the blackboard. The BTService_ScheduleCheck runs as a fallback/safety and ensures the blackboard is synced.
Behavior Tree MoveTo uses TargetActor; after arrival it runs the PerformActivity task (which calls the ActivityInterface on the pawn to allow the pawn to play anims, and the task waits ActivityDuration seconds).
WBP_ScheduleDebug polls the GameState and the NPC's CurrentActivity variable and displays them.

Corrected Header (final version)
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/GameStateBase.h"
#include "NH_GameState.generated.h"

DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_TwoParams(
    FOnNHMinuteChanged,
    int32, Hour,
    int32, Minute
);

/**
 * Global game clock. Ticks in minutes and broadcasts minute changes.
 */
UCLASS()
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_GameState : public AGameStateBase
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    ANH_GameState();

    virtual void Tick(float DeltaSeconds) override;
    virtual void BeginPlay() override;

    // Current in-game time
    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentHour = 6;

    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Time")
    int32 CurrentMinute = 0;

    // In-game minutes advanced per real second.
    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category="Time")
    float TimeScale = 1.0f;

    // Fired after time updates
    UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable, Category="Time")
    FOnNHMinuteChanged OnMinuteChanged;

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Time")
    void SetTime(int32 Hour, int32 Minute);

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Time")
    void GetTime(int32& OutHour, int32& OutMinute) const;

protected:
    float MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;
};

The Missing .cpp (This Is the Engine)

Create NH_GameState.cpp and paste this exactly.

#include "NH_GameState.h"

ANH_GameState::ANH_GameState()
{
    PrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = true;
    PrimaryActorTick.bStartWithTickEnabled = true;
}

void ANH_GameState::BeginPlay()
{
    Super::BeginPlay();
    MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;
}

void ANH_GameState::Tick(float DeltaSeconds)
{
    Super::Tick(DeltaSeconds);

    if (TimeScale <= 0.f)
    {
        return;
    }

    MinuteAccumulator += DeltaSeconds * TimeScale;

    while (MinuteAccumulator >= 1.0f)
    {
        MinuteAccumulator -= 1.0f;
        CurrentMinute++;

        if (CurrentMinute >= 60)
        {
            CurrentMinute = 0;
            CurrentHour = (CurrentHour + 1) % 24;
        }

        OnMinuteChanged.Broadcast(CurrentHour, CurrentMinute);
    }
}

void ANH_GameState::SetTime(int32 Hour, int32 Minute)
{
    CurrentHour = FMath::Clamp(Hour, 0, 23);
    CurrentMinute = FMath::Clamp(Minute, 0, 59);
    MinuteAccumulator = 0.0f;

    OnMinuteChanged.Broadcast(CurrentHour, CurrentMinute);
}

void ANH_GameState::GetTime(int32& OutHour, int32& OutMinute) const
{
    OutHour = CurrentHour;
    OutMinute = CurrentMinute;
}

Why This Version Is Correct

Uses while, not if, so low FPS doesn’t desync time

Broadcasts after time changes

Safe against TimeScale = 0

Blueprint-friendly

Deterministic

This clock is now authoritative enough to run:

NPC schedules

Shift changes

Lockdowns

Meals

Story triggers

1) Console Commands (So You Can Bend Time Without Rebuilding Reality)
You should never test schedules by waiting around like a civilian.

Add to ScheduleManager.cpp
void AScheduleManager::ForceTime(int32 Hour, int32 Minute)
{
    if (!HasAuthority()) return;

    if (ANH_GameState* GS = GetWorld()->GetGameState<ANH_GameState>())
    {
        GS->SetTime(Hour, Minute);
        RefreshAllSchedules(Hour, Minute);
    }
}

void AScheduleManager::ForceMinuteTick()
{
    if (!HasAuthority()) return;

    if (ANH_GameState* GS = GetWorld()->GetGameState<ANH_GameState>())
    {
        int32 H, M;
        GS->GetTime(H, M);
        M++;
        if (M >= 60) { M = 0; H = (H + 1) % 24; }
        GS->SetTime(H, M);
        RefreshAllSchedules(H, M);
    }
}
Usage in PIE

ForceMinuteTick
No rebuild. No UI. Just authority.

2) Lockdown Override (Because Prison Without Lockdown Is Cosplay)

Add to ScheduleManager.cpp
void AScheduleManager::StartLockdown()
{
    if (!HasAuthority()) return;
    bLockdownActive = true;
    ForceLockdownTargets();
}

void AScheduleManager::EndLockdown()
{
    if (!HasAuthority()) return;
    bLockdownActive = false;

    int32 H, M;
    if (ANH_GameState* GS = GetWorld()->GetGameState<ANH_GameState>())
    {
        GS->GetTime(H, M);
        RefreshAllSchedules(H, M);
    }
}
Modify RefreshAllSchedules
void AScheduleManager::RefreshAllSchedules(int32 Hour, int32 Minute)
{
    for (TActorIterator<AActor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        if (UNH_ScheduleComponent* Comp =
            It->FindComponentByClass<UNH_ScheduleComponent>())
        {
            if (bLockdownActive)
            {
                Comp->ForceOverride(LockdownTargetPointName, "Lockdown");
            }
            else
            {
                Comp->RefreshScheduleAtTime(Hour, Minute);
            }
        }
    }
}
Add to NH_ScheduleComponent
void ForceOverride(FName TargetPoint, FName Activity);

1️⃣ ADoor ACTOR (AUTHORITATIVE, REPLICATED)
ADoor.h
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"
#include "Door.generated.h"

DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockStateChanged, bool, bLocked);

UCLASS()
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ADoor : public AActor
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    ADoor();

    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)
    UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;

    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_Locked)
    bool bIsLocked = false;

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)
    FOnDoorLockStateChanged OnDoorLockStateChanged;

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void LockDoor();

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void UnlockDoor();

protected:
    virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;

    UFUNCTION()
    void OnRep_Locked();

    void ApplyLockState();
};

ADoor.cpp
#include "Door.h"
#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"

ADoor::ADoor()
{
    bReplicates = true;

    DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>("DoorMesh");
    RootComponent = DoorMesh;

    DoorMesh->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");
}

void ADoor::LockDoor()
{
    if (!bIsLocked)
    {
        bIsLocked = true;
        ApplyLockState();
    }
}

void ADoor::UnlockDoor()
{
    if (bIsLocked)
    {
        bIsLocked = false;
        ApplyLockState();
    }
}

void ADoor::ApplyLockState()
{
    DoorMesh->SetCollisionEnabled(
        bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics
                  : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision
    );

    OnDoorLockStateChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);
}

void ADoor::OnRep_Locked()
{
    ApplyLockState();
}

void ADoor::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const
{
    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);
    DOREPLIFETIME(ADoor, bIsLocked);
}


This door:

Blocks movement when locked

Replicates cleanly

Broadcasts state changes for animation/UI

Requires no NavMesh rebuild

Collision blocking is enough. Keep it simple.

3️⃣ WIRE DOORS INTO LOCKDOWN (ScheduleManager or GameRules)

Add this to ScheduleManager.cpp (or GameRules if that’s your authority):

#include "Door.h"
#include "EngineUtils.h"

void AScheduleManager::StartLockdown()
{
    bLockdownActive = true;

    for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))
        {
            It->LockDoor();
        }
    }
}

void AScheduleManager::EndLockdown()
{
    bLockdownActive = false;

    for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))
        {
            It->UnlockDoor();
        }
    }
}

PART 1: Door Actor (C++ Backbone)
Create C++ class

Parent: AActor
Name: NH_Door

NH_Door.h
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"
#include "NH_Door.generated.h"

DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockChanged, bool, bLocked);

UCLASS()
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_Door : public AActor
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    ANH_Door();

    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)
    UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;

    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)
    UBoxComponent* Blocker;

    UPROPERTY(ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_LockState, BlueprintReadOnly)
    bool bIsLocked = false;

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)
    FOnDoorLockChanged OnDoorLockChanged;

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void LockDoor();

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void UnlockDoor();

protected:
    virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;

    UFUNCTION()
    void OnRep_LockState();
};

NH_Door.cpp
#include "NH_Door.h"
#include "Components/StaticMeshComponent.h"
#include "Components/BoxComponent.h"
#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"

ANH_Door::ANH_Door()
{
    bReplicates = true;

    DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(TEXT("DoorMesh"));
    RootComponent = DoorMesh;

    Blocker = CreateDefaultSubobject<UBoxComponent>(TEXT("Blocker"));
    Blocker->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);
    Blocker->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");
    Blocker->SetHiddenInGame(true);
}

void ANH_Door::LockDoor()
{
    if (!bIsLocked)
    {
        bIsLocked = true;
        Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics);
        OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(true);
    }
}

void ANH_Door::UnlockDoor()
{
    if (bIsLocked)
    {
        bIsLocked = false;
        Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);
        OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(false);
    }
}

void ANH_Door::OnRep_LockState()
{
    Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(
        bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision
    );

    OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);
}

void ANH_Door::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const
{
    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);
    DOREPLIFETIME(ANH_Door, bIsLocked);
}


What this does

Blocker physically blocks movement + NavMesh

No teleporting NPCs

No rebuilding nav every time

Works in PIE and multiplayer

PART 2: Hook Doors Into Lockdown

You already have GameRules / ScheduleManager. We extend it.

In ScheduleManager.h

Add:

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
void SetLockdown(bool bEnable);

In ScheduleManager.cpp
#include "NH_Door.h"

void AScheduleManager::SetLockdown(bool bEnable)
{
    for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        if (bEnable)
        {
            It->LockDoor();
        }
        else
        {
            It->UnlockDoor();
        }
    }
}

ViolationCheck.
bool IsViolatingSchedule(ACharacter* Inmate, UNH_ScheduleComponent* Schedule)
{
    if (! Inmate || !Schedule) return false;

    AActor* CurrentTarget = Schedule->GetCurrentTargetActor();
    if (!CurrentTarget) return false;
These are called by guards every few seconds (via BT Service or tick).

  │   │   ├─ If Still Violating: Pursue
  │   │   └─ If Still Violating: Force Detain (override schedule to holding cell)
  │   │
  │   └─ Sequence: Patrol (default)
  │       ├─ MoveTo Patrol Points
  │       └─ Wait

PART 1: Door Actor (C++ Backbone)
Create C++ class

Parent: AActor
Name: NH_Door

NH_Door.h
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"
#include "NH_Door.generated.h"

DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockChanged, bool, bLocked);

UCLASS()
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_Door : public AActor
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    ANH_Door();

    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)
    UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;

    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)
    UBoxComponent* Blocker;

    UPROPERTY(ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_LockState, BlueprintReadOnly)
    bool bIsLocked = false;

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)
    FOnDoorLockChanged OnDoorLockChanged;

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void LockDoor();

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void UnlockDoor();

protected:
    virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;

    UFUNCTION()
    void OnRep_LockState();
};

NH_Door.cpp
#include "NH_Door.h"
#include "Components/StaticMeshComponent.h"
#include "Components/BoxComponent.h"
#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"

ANH_Door::ANH_Door()
{
    bReplicates = true;

    DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(TEXT("DoorMesh"));
    RootComponent = DoorMesh;

    Blocker = CreateDefaultSubobject<UBoxComponent>(TEXT("Blocker"));
    Blocker->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);
    Blocker->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");
    Blocker->SetHiddenInGame(true);
}

void ANH_Door::LockDoor()
{
    if (!bIsLocked)
    {
        bIsLocked = true;
        Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics);
        OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(true);
    }
}

void ANH_Door::UnlockDoor()
{
    if (bIsLocked)
    {
        bIsLocked = false;
        Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);
        OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(false);
    }
}

void ANH_Door::OnRep_LockState()
{
    Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(
        bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision
    );

    OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);
}

void ANH_Door::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const
{
    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);
    DOREPLIFETIME(ANH_Door, bIsLocked);
}


What this does

Blocker physically blocks movement + NavMesh

No teleporting NPCs

No rebuilding nav every time

Works in PIE and multiplayer

PART 2: Hook Doors Into Lockdown

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
void SetLockdown(bool bEnable);

In ScheduleManager.cpp
#include "NH_Door.h"

void AScheduleManager::SetLockdown(bool bEnable)
{
    for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        if (bEnable)
        {
            It->LockDoor();
        }
        else
        {
            It->UnlockDoor();
        }
    }
}

STEP 3: SAVE IMPLEMENTATION
ScheduleManager.cpp (core logic)
#include "SaveGame_Nyghtshade.h"
#include "Kismet/GameplayStatics.h"
#include "NH_GameState.h"
#include "NH_Door.h"
#include "NH_ScheduleComponent.h"

void AScheduleManager::SavePrison()
{
    USaveGame_Nyghtshade* Save =
        Cast<USaveGame_Nyghtshade>(
            UGameplayStatics::CreateSaveGameObject(USaveGame_Nyghtshade::StaticClass())
        );

    // Time
    if (ANH_GameState* GS = GetWorld()->GetGameState<ANH_GameState>())
    {
        Save->Hour = GS->CurrentHour;
        Save->Minute = GS->CurrentMinute;
    }

    // Lockdown
    Save->bLockdownActive = bLockdownActive;

    // Doors
    for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        FDoorSaveData Data;
        Data.DoorName = It->GetFName();
        Data.bIsLocked = It->bIsLocked;
        Save->Doors.Add(Data);
    }

    // NPCs
    for (TActorIterator<ACharacter> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        if (UNH_ScheduleComponent* Schedule = It->FindComponentByClass<UNH_ScheduleComponent>())
        {
            FNPCSaveData NPC;
            NPC.NPCName = It->GetFName();
            NPC.CurrentActivity = Schedule->GetCurrentActivityName();
            if (AActor* Target = Schedule->GetCurrentTargetActor())
            {
                NPC.CurrentTargetPoint = Target->GetFName();
            }
            Save->NPCs.Add(NPC);
        }
    }

    UGameplayStatics::SaveGameToSlot(Save, TEXT("NyghtshadeSlot"), 0);
}

STEP 4: LOAD IMPLEMENTATION
void AScheduleManager::LoadPrison()
{
    USaveGame_Nyghtshade* Save =
        Cast<USaveGame_Nyghtshade>(
            UGameplayStatics::LoadGameFromSlot(TEXT("NyghtshadeSlot"), 0)
        );

    if (!Save) return;

    // Restore time
    if (ANH_GameState* GS = GetWorld()->GetGameState<ANH_GameState>())
    {
        GS->SetTime(Save->Hour, Save->Minute);
    }

    // Restore lockdown
    SetLockdown(Save->bLockdownActive);

    // Restore doors
    for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        for (const FDoorSaveData& DoorData : Save->Doors)
        {
            if (It->GetFName() == DoorData.DoorName)
            {
                DoorData.bIsLocked ? It->LockDoor() : It->UnlockDoor();
            }
        }
    }

    // Restore NPC schedules
    for (TActorIterator<ACharacter> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
    {
        if (UNH_ScheduleComponent* Schedule = It->FindComponentByClass<UNH_ScheduleComponent>())
        {
            for (const FNPCSaveData& NPC : Save->NPCs)
            {
                if (It->GetFName() == NPC.NPCName)
                {
                    Schedule->ForceActivity(NPC.CurrentActivity, NPC.CurrentTargetPoint);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}


This does not restart behavior trees. It restores state, then lets AI continue naturally.

That’s the key difference between a save and a reset.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

UCLASS(ClassGroup=(Authority), meta=(BlueprintSpawnableComponent))
class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API UInmateAuthorityComponent : public UActorComponent
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    UInmateAuthorityComponent();

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Replicated)
    int32 AuthorityLevel; // 0–5

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Replicated)
    TArray<FViolationRecord> ViolationHistory;

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void RegisterViolation(
        EViolationType Type,
        int32 Severity,
        FName ReportingGuard,
        const FString& Context
    );

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)
    void DecayAuthority(float DeltaGameTime);

protected:
    virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& Out) const override;
};

InmateAuthorityComponent.cpp
#include "InmateAuthorityComponent.h"
#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"

UInmateAuthorityComponent::UInmateAuthorityComponent()
{
    SetIsReplicatedByDefault(true);
    AuthorityLevel = 0;
}

void UInmateAuthorityComponent::RegisterViolation(
    EViolationType Type,
    int32 Severity,
    FName ReportingGuard,
    const FString& Context)
{
    FViolationRecord Record;
    Record.Type = Type;
    Record.Severity = Severity;
    Record.ReportingGuard = ReportingGuard;
    Record.Context = Context;
    Record.GameTimeStamp = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds();

    ViolationHistory.Add(Record);

    AuthorityLevel = FMath::Clamp(AuthorityLevel + Severity, 0, 5);
}

void UInmateAuthorityComponent::DecayAuthority(float DeltaGameTime)
{
    if (AuthorityLevel > 0 && DeltaGameTime > 600.f) // 10 min clean behavior
    {
        AuthorityLevel--;
    }
}

void UInmateAuthorityComponent::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& Out) const
{
    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(Out);
    DOREPLIFETIME(UInmateAuthorityComponent, AuthorityLevel);
    DOREPLIFETIME(UInmateAuthorityComponent, ViolationHistory);
}

GuardEscalationComponent.cpp
#include "GuardEscalationComponent.h"
#include "InmateAuthorityComponent.h"
#include "NH_ScheduleComponent.h"
#include "GameFramework/Character.h"

void UGuardEscalationComponent::EvaluateInmate(ACharacter* Inmate)
{
    if (!Inmate) return;

    auto* Authority = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateAuthorityComponent>();
    auto* Schedule  = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UNH_ScheduleComponent>();

    if (!Authority || !Schedule) return;

    if (!Schedule->IsAtScheduledLocation())
    {
        Authority->RegisterViolation(
            EViolationType::Schedule,
            1,
            GetOwner()->GetFName(),
            TEXT("Not at scheduled location")
        );

        Escalate(Inmate, Authority->AuthorityLevel);
    }
}

void UGuardEscalationComponent::Escalate(ACharacter* Inmate, int32 Level)
{
    if (Level < AuthorityThreshold)
    {
        IssueWarning(Inmate);
        return;
    }

    if (Level >= 3)
    {
        // Phase 2 hook: Detention / Seg
        Inmate->GetCharacterMovement()->MaxWalkSpeed = 120.f;
    }
}

void UGuardEscalationComponent::IssueWarning(ACharacter* Inmate)
{
    UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("Guard %s issued warning to %s"),
        *GetOwner()->GetName(),
        *Inmate->GetName()
    );

JudicialPunishmentComponent.cpp

#include "JudicialPunishmentComponent.h"
#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"

void UJudicialPunishmentComponent::ApplyPunishment(
    EPunishmentType Type,
    float Duration,
    bool bParoleEligible,
    const FString& Reason,
    FName Issuer)
{
    FPunishmentRecord Record;
    Record.Type = Type;
    Record.Duration = Duration;
    Record.TimeServed = 0.f;
    Record.StartGameTime = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds();
    Record.bParoleEligible = bParoleEligible;
    Record.Reason = Reason;
    Record.IssuingAuthority = Issuer;

    ActivePunishments.Add(Record);
}

void UJudicialPunishmentComponent::UpdatePunishments(float DeltaGameTime)
{
    for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)
    {
        ActivePunishments[i].TimeServed += DeltaGameTime;
        if (ActivePunishments[i].TimeServed >= ActivePunishments[i].Duration)
        {
            ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);
        }
    }
}

EPunishmentType UJudicialPunishmentComponent::GetHighestActivePunishment() const
{
    EPunishmentType Highest = EPunishmentType::None;
    for (const auto& P : ActivePunishments)
    {
        if ((uint8)P.Type > (uint8)Highest)
        {
            Highest = P.Type;
        }
    }
    return Highest;
}

void UJudicialPunishmentComponent::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(
    TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& Out) const
{
    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(Out);
    DOREPLIFETIME(UJudicialPunishmentComponent, ActivePunishments);
}

InmateJudicialComponent.cpp
#include "InmateJudicialComponent.h"
#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"

void UInmateJudicialComponent::SentenceInmate(
    EPunishmentType Type,
    float Duration,
    const FString& Reason)
{
    FPunishmentRecord Record;
    Record.Type = Type;
    Record.Duration = Duration;
    Record.TimeServed = 0.f;
    Record.StartGameTime = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds();
    Record.bEligibleForReview = (Duration > 0);
    Record.Reason = Reason;

    ActivePunishments.Add(Record);
    OnPunishmentAdded.Broadcast(Record);
}

void UInmateJudicialComponent::TickPunishments(float DeltaSeconds)
{
    for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)
    {
        auto& P = ActivePunishments[i];
        if (P.Duration < 0.f) continue;

        P.TimeServed += DeltaSeconds;
        if (P.TimeServed >= P.Duration)
        {
            ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);
        }
    }
}

bool UInmateJudicialComponent::IsInSegregation() const
{
    for (const auto& P : ActivePunishments)
    {
        if (P.Type == EPunishmentType::SolitarySegregation ||
            P.Type == EPunishmentType::IndefiniteSegregation)
        {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

void UInmateJudicialComponent::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(
    TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& Out) const
{
    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(Out);
    DOREPLIFETIME(UInmateJudicialComponent, ActivePunishments);
}

PHASE 3.2 — SAVE MANAGER (THE CLERK)
