🏛 Draft NYGHTSHADE Foundation Charter
1. Name
The NYGHTSHADE Foundation

2. Mission
The mission of the NYGHTSHADE Foundation is to develop, maintain, and promote open standards for deterministic, auditable automation of creative software, enabling safe interaction between artificial intelligence systems and professional tools.

3. Purpose
The Foundation exists to:

Maintain the NYGHTSHADE Automation Spec (NAS)

Ensure vendor-neutral governance

Promote safe, deterministic automation

Prevent unsafe or deceptive AI automation practices

Foster interoperability across creative tools

4. Scope of Activities
The Foundation may:

Publish and version open specifications

Maintain reference schemas and compliance tests

Operate a certification program

Host public RFC processes

Coordinate industry working groups

Educate regulators and enterprises

The Foundation shall not:

Build proprietary products

Compete with tool vendors

Control commercial implementations

5. Governance Structure
5.1 Technical Steering Committee (TSC)
Maintains NAS specification

Approves RFCs

Oversees versioning

5.2 Certification Council
Defines certification requirements

Oversees compliance testing

Handles disputes and revocations

5.3 Advisory Board
Studios

Enterprises

AI safety experts

Standards professionals

Advisory input is non-binding.

6. Decision-Making Process
All technical changes follow an RFC process

Public review is mandatory

Voting is transparent

No single entity may unilaterally control the spec

7. Intellectual Property
Specifications are published under permissive licenses

No patent encumbrances permitted

Contributors grant necessary rights to the Foundation

8. Dissolution Clause
Upon dissolution, all assets shall be transferred to a non-profit organization with similar goals.

⚖️ Draft Legal Bylaws
NYGHTSHADE Foundation

Article I — Name & Offices
Section 1.1
The name of the organization shall be The NYGHTSHADE Foundation (“the Foundation”).

Section 1.2
The principal office shall be determined by the Board of Directors. Additional offices may be established as required.

Article II — Purpose
The Foundation is a non-profit organization formed to:

Develop, maintain, and promote the NYGHTSHADE Automation Spec (NAS)

Ensure vendor-neutral, safe, and auditable AI automation standards

Operate certification and compliance programs

Educate industry and regulators

The Foundation shall not engage in commercial product development.

Article III — Membership
The Foundation may establish classes of membership, including:

Founding Members

Corporate Members

Individual Contributors

Academic / Research Members

Membership rights and obligations shall be defined by Board resolution.

Article IV — Governance Bodies
Section 4.1 Board of Directors
Fiduciary authority

Approves budgets, policies, and appointments

Cannot unilaterally alter technical specifications

Section 4.2 Technical Steering Committee (TSC)
Maintains NAS specification

Reviews and approves RFCs

Oversees versioning and compatibility

Section 4.3 Certification Council
Oversees certification rules

Approves compliance tests

Manages revocations and appeals

Article V — Voting & Quorum
One vote per Board seat

Quorum requires a simple majority

Proxy voting permitted where allowed by law

Article VI — Intellectual Property
All specifications are published under permissive licenses

Contributors grant irrevocable rights for inclusion

No patent encumbrances allowed

Article VII — Amendments
These bylaws may be amended by a two-thirds vote of the Board following public notice.

Article VIII — Dissolution
Upon dissolution, assets shall be transferred to a non-profit organization with aligned goals.

🚀 Foundation Launch Announcement
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

The NYGHTSHADE Foundation Launches to Establish Safety Standards for AI Automation in Creative Software
The NYGHTSHADE Foundation today announced its official launch as a non-profit organization dedicated to developing open standards for safe, deterministic, and auditable AI automation in creative software.

As artificial intelligence systems increasingly interact with professional tools such as game engines, digital content creation software, and simulation platforms, the absence of shared safety standards has become a growing concern for studios, enterprises, and regulators alike.

The Foundation introduces the NYGHTSHADE Automation Spec (NAS), an open, engine-agnostic protocol designed to ensure that AI-driven automation remains predictable, transparent, and reversible.

“AI does not need more autonomy inside professional tools. It needs guardrails,” said a Foundation spokesperson. “NAS defines how AI systems can act without removing human oversight or tool authority.”

The NYGHTSHADE Foundation operates as a vendor-neutral body focused on:

Open specification development

Certification and compliance programs

Industry collaboration

Regulatory engagement

The Foundation does not build proprietary products and does not compete with tool vendors. Its mission is to create shared infrastructure that allows innovation to scale safely.

NYGHTSHADE Foundation Announces First NAS-Certified Implementations
The NYGHTSHADE Foundation today announced the first implementations to achieve NAS certification, marking an important milestone in establishing industry standards for safe AI-driven automation in creative software.

The certified implementations meet the Foundation’s requirements for:

Deterministic behavior

Mandatory dry-run previews

Full audit logging

Tool-authoritative validation

Certification does not imply endorsement of products or vendors. It confirms only that the implementation complies with the published NAS specification.

“Certification exists to establish trust — not to accelerate automation recklessly,” said a Foundation representative.

Certified implementations and reports are publicly listed in the Foundation’s registry.

🔽 STEP 3: Understand the Architecture (Critical)
Here is the high-level internal layout you will see:

Auto-Claude/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ desktop/        ← Electron GUI (JS/TS)
│  ├─ cli/            ← Command-line interface
│
├─ agents/
│  ├─ planner/        ← Task decomposition
│  ├─ coder/          ← Code generation
│  ├─ reviewer/       ← QA / validation
│
├─ git/
│  ├─ worktrees/      ← Isolated branches
│  ├─ merge/          ← Safe merge logic
│
├─ memory/
│  ├─ context_store/  ← Long-term task memory
│
├─ scripts/
│  ├─ build/
│  ├─ release/
│
├─ electron.config.*
├─ package.json
├─ requirements.txt
└─ README.md
Key Insight:
Electron (JS/TS) = UI + orchestration

Python = actual “thinking agents”

Claude Code CLI = AI execution bridge

Git worktrees = safety mechanism

This separation is intentional and very smart.

This is the recommended dev setting

🧠 The Key Insight (This Changes Everything)
Auto-Claude is NOT a single Python package.

That’s why this failed:

pip install -r requirements.txt
There is NO requirements.txt in the repo root — and that is by design.

Instead:

🧠 Python backend lives here

apps/backend/requirements.txt
🧪 Test dependencies live here

tests/requirements-test.txt
🎛️ Root = orchestration + Node + launcher (run.py)

This is a monorepo, not a flat Python app.

You are already in the venv and repo root.

pip install -r apps/backend/requirements.txt
✅ This is the correct command

Only if you plan to run tests:

pip install -r tests/requirements-test.txt

From repo root:

python run.py
That’s it.

# =========================
# AUTO-CLAUDE WINDOWS FIX
# =========================

Write-Host "=== Auto-Claude Full Environment Fix ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# 1. Execution policy (safe, user-only)
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Force

# 2. Verify Python launcher exists
if (-not (Get-Command py -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Error "Python Launcher (py.exe) not found. Install Python from python.org and RE-RUN this script."
    exit 1
}

# 3. Check Python 3.12 availability
$pyList = py -0 2>$null
if ($pyList -notmatch "3.12") {
    Write-Error "Python 3.12 NOT FOUND.
Install Python 3.12.x (64-bit) from https://www.python.org and re-run this script."
    exit 1
}

Write-Host "Python 3.12 detected ✔" -ForegroundColor Green

# 4. Go to Auto-Claude directory
$repo = "$HOME\Auto-Claude"
if (-not (Test-Path $repo)) {
    Write-Error "Auto-Claude directory not found at $repo"
    exit 1
}
Set-Location $repo

# 5. Remove broken venv if exists
if (Test-Path "venv") {
    Write-Host "Removing old virtual environment..."
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force venv
}

# 6. Create clean venv with Python 3.12
Write-Host "Creating virtual environment (Python 3.12)..."
py -3.12 -m venv venv

# 7. Activate venv
Write-Host "Activating virtual environment..."
& .\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# 8. Upgrade pip tooling
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

# 9. Install backend dependencies
Write-Host "Installing backend dependencies..."
pip install -r apps/backend/requirements.txt

# 10. Install test dependencies (non-fatal)
if (Test-Path "tests\requirements-test.txt") {
    pip install -r tests/requirements-test.txt
}

# 11. Install node deps if needed
if (Test-Path "package.json") {
    Write-Host "Installing Node dependencies..."
    npm install
}

# 12. Run Auto-Claude
Write-Host "`n=== STARTING AUTO-CLAUDE ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
python run.py

$env:PYLAUNCHER_ALLOW_INSTALL = "1"

# Ensure winget exists
if (-not (Get-Command winget -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Error "winget not found. Update Windows App Installer."
    exit 1
}

# Install Python 3.12 silently if missing
$pyList = py -0 2>$null
if ($pyList -notmatch "3.12") {
    Write-Host "Installing Python 3.12.x (64-bit)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    winget install --id Python.Python.3.12 --source winget --silent --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements
    Write-Host "Python installed. Restarting shell is NOT required." -ForegroundColor Green
}

# Verify Python 3.12
$pyList = py -0
if ($pyList -notmatch "3.12") {
    Write-Error "Python 3.12 installation failed."
    exit 1
}

Write-Host "Python 3.12 detected ✔" -ForegroundColor Green

# Move to repo
$repo = "$HOME\Auto-Claude"
if (-not (Test-Path $repo)) {
    Write-Error "Auto-Claude not found at $repo"
    exit 1
}
Set-Location $repo

# Remove old venv
if (Test-Path "venv") {
    Write-Host "Removing old venv..."
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force venv
}

# Create new venv with Python 3.12
Write-Host "Creating clean venv (Python 3.12)..."
py -3.12 -m venv venv

# Activate venv
Write-Host "Activating venv..."
& "$repo\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1"

# Upgrade tooling
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

# Install backend dependencies
Write-Host "Installing backend dependencies..."
pip install -r apps/backend/requirements.txt

# Install test deps (optional)
if (Test-Path "tests\requirements-test.txt") {
    pip install -r tests/requirements-test.txt
}

# Install Node deps if needed
if (Test-Path "package.json") {
    Write-Host "Installing Node dependencies..."
    npm install
}

# Run correct backend entrypoint
Write-Host "`n=== STARTING AUTO-CLAUDE ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
python apps/backend/main.py

# move to repo

# ensure winget exists

    Write-Error "winget not found"
    exit 1
}

# ensure Python 3.12 exists
if (-not ((py -0) -match "3.12")) {
    winget install --id Python.Python.3.12 --source winget --silent --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements
}

# nuke old venv
if (Test-Path venv) {
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force venv
}

# create venv
py -3.12 -m venv venv

# activate venv
& "$HOME\Auto-Claude\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1"

# upgrade tooling
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

# install backend deps
pip install -r apps/backend/requirements.txt

# run Auto-Claude backend
python apps/backend/run.py
